content_of_post_to_answer: Do you really get used to shifting gears in a manual car, or does it always take some of your attention away from driving?
answer: The interesting part is that you never really stop using attention; you change what kind of attention is required. Early on, shifting gears is a conscious task competing with steering, mirrors, and traffic. With practice, it becomes procedural memory, like walking while talking. But skilled drivers still pay attention to gear choice in unusual situations—hills, overtaking, slippery roads—because automation handles the routine, not the unexpected. Mastery is not doing more things consciously; it is moving common actions out of consciousness so your mind can focus on what actually matters.
